title: Difficulty breathing
reference: NASA Flight Rules: Respiratory Distress, Airway Emergencies & ISS Environmental Life Support System (ECLSS) Protocols.

q1.text: Is there audible stridor, harsh gasping, or is the crew member unable to speak even single words?

i_upper.text: ACUTE UPPER AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION / SEVERE DISTRESS: Clear oropharynx with suction. Insert supraglottic airway (i-gel) or prepare bag-valve-mask with 100% O2.

t_airway.text: Deliver rescue ventilation with high-flow O2 for 60 seconds while monitoring chest rise and pulse oximetry.

q2.text: Is pulse oximetry SpO2 < 95% or is the module cabin CO2 reading > 3.0 mmHg?

i_hypox.text: HYPOXIA / HYPERCAPNIA ALERT: Don Emergency Portable Breathing Apparatus (PBA) with 100% O2. Inspect module air diffusers for stagnant CO2 pockets.

t_o2.text: Administer high-flow O2 for 2 minutes while verifying pulse oximeter waveform and respiratory rate.

q_o2_resp.text: After 2 minutes of 100% O2, has SpO2 risen to >= 96% and respiratory rate stabilized?

i_o2_ok.text: OXYGENATION RECOVERED: Maintain low-flow O2. Inspect module ventilation fans and life support Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly (CDRA).

i_o2_fail.text: REFRACTORY HYPOXIA: Suspect pulmonary edema, pneumothorax, or toxic inhalation. Prepare Albuterol inhaler (4 puffs) and dexamethasone.

q3.text: Does the astronaut report sudden chest tightness or wheezing during or immediately after exercise/work?

i_broncho.text: BRONCHOSPASM / EXERCISE-INDUCED ASTHMA: Administer 2 puffs of Albuterol aerosol inhaler via spacer. Seat upright and guide slow exhalations.

i_hypervent.text: ANXIETY / HYPERVENTILATION: Vital signs nominal. Guide slow diaphragmatic breathing (4s inhale, 7s hold, 8s exhale) in quiet module.

end_monitor.text: Respiratory status stabilized. Continue continuous SpO2 pulse oximetry monitoring for 2 hours and record incident in log.

end_escalate.text: RESPIRATORY CRISIS ESCALATED: Emergency consultation active with Flight Surgeon. Cabin life support diagnostics in progress.
